MAX_PATH().notice: Bound on the checkpoints a run reads (the oracle writes at most one per block).

MAX_SEGMENT_MOVE().notice: A single checkpoint-to-checkpoint move is clamped to +/-20 % before scaling.

SCALE().notice: Multipliers are fixed point with 6 decimals: 1_000_000 = the stake back.

ladder().notice: The ladder in tenths of x: 10, 15, 20 ... 40.

moveScale().notice: Game scale: how many times a real price move counts, before leverage.

multipliers(uint256,uint256,uint256,uint.notice: Value / stake (6 decimals) of a long and of a short that entered at checkpoint         `entryIndex` at time `start` and left at checkpoint `exitIndex`, the ladder capped         at `capStep`. Index bounds (not times) make the result reproducible by anyone, even         when another checkpoint lands later in the block of a cash out.

userdoc.notice: The rules of a Siroclimb run, in clear: given a market's oracle checkpoints between a         run's entry and its exit, what would a long and what would a short have made? Every move between two consecutive checkpoints counts `moveScale` times (the game scale) at the leverage of the ladder step the checkpoint lands on: 1x, 1.5x, 2x ... 4x, one step every 6 seconds from the start. PnL adds up on the stake, like a position of constant notional; when it reaches -100 % the coin falls and the run is worth 0 for good. Both results are public (anyone can recompute them from the oracle); which one a player gets depends on their encrypted side, which only the game contract combines on ciphertexts.
